chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hajjal, from Tha'laba, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam)
key_terms.الْقَابِلَةُ: The midwife, a female birth attendant
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةٌ: Trusted, reliable, or trustworthy (feminine form of aman)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a midwife's testimony in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the midwife (qabula) as a primary witness of trust (ma'muna), particularly crucial for determining lineage and paternity in the absence of other evidence. Scholars highlight that this reliability extends to her testimony regarding the timing of birth and physical characteristics, making her a key figure in family law and inheritance cases.
